results.title: Archaeologists discover more than 150 new Nazca lines in Peru
excerpts:
# Archaeologists discover more than 150 new Nazca lines in Peru
The researchers from Peru and Japan discovered 168 previously unknown geoglyphs that Indigenous people created near the city of Nazca – including outlines of humans, birds, killer whales, felines, and snakes.
It’s still unknown why they created this type of drawing, and why they did so many, but scientists hope the new findings will help to bring some light to the long mystery.

...

> “Adding the newly discovered 168 geoglyphs to the 190 geoglyphs discovered until 2018 results in a total of 358 geoglyphs,” [the statement reads](https://www.yamagata-u.ac.jp/en/information/info/20221208/) .

...

## The mystery of the Nazca lines
The newly discovered [line drawings](https://www.zmescience.com/research/archaeologists-discover-old-cat-figure-in-nazca-537684562/) are, on average, between two and six meters in length and can be seen from the ground, but are much more spectacular when viewed from the air.

...

### Related **Posts**
Now, the team from Peru and Japan is working on developing artificial intelligence that can detect geoglyphs by analyzing aerial images. While they didn’t use this to find the 168 geoglyphs, they hope to use the newly found drawing to “teach” the system to find more.

...

Researchers have discovered 190 figures in the area since 2004. But the vastness of the terrain they cover has complicated efforts to conserve the heritage site.

results.title: Scientists Discover 168 Mysterious Nazca Geoglyphs in The Desert Sands of Peru : ScienceAlert
excerpts:
# Scientists Discover 168 Mysterious Nazca Geoglyphs in The Desert Sands of Peru
Drone surveys and aerial images in southern Peru have now identified 168 new geoglyphs in the Nazca Lines [World Heritage Site](https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/700) , with roughly 50 of these large-scale geographical drawings depicting human-like figures.

...

In 2019, a new Nazca line design was [actually discovered by AI](https://www.sciencealert.com/over-140-mysterious-geoglyphs-discovered-within-the-ancient-nazca-lines) .

...

The lines have been interpreted in numerous ways over the decades, but the most common explanation is that they were meant for gods in the sky who were looking down on humans.

...

In 1994, when a part of the Nazca desert was designated a World Heritage Site, [only about 30 'geoglyphs' had been found](https://www.yamagata-u.ac.jp/en/files/7615/7381/2393/PRESS_RELEASE_nasca191115EN.pdf) , and they were mostly of plants and animals.

...

By 2019, archaeologists had found [nearly 200 geoglyphs in total](https://www.sciencealert.com/over-140-mysterious-geoglyphs-discovered-within-the-ancient-nazca-lines) , several of which depicted humanoid figures.

...

With permission from the Peruvian Ministry of Culture, scientists at Yamagata have made it their mission to tally as many of these mysterious designs as they can.

# AI uncovers hundreds of new Nazca geoglyphs in breakthrough discovery

results.title: Nazca Line Discoveries in Peru Suggest the Mysterious Geoglyphs Are Pervasive | HISTORY
excerpts:
# Nazca Line Discoveries in Peru Suggest the Mysterious Geoglyphs Are Pervasive
In November 2019, researchers announced the detection of 143 new geoglyphs on southern Peru’s Nazca plain. The geoglyphs date from 100 B.C. to A.D. 300, and range in size from about 16 to 330 feet across (for comparison, the Statue of Liberty is 305 feet tall).

...

Researchers from Yamagata University in Japan detected 142 of the 143 geoglyphs by performing fieldwork and analyzing high-resolution 3D data, and they detected the final glyph using artificial intelligence in partnership with IBM Japan.
The 143 geoglyphs add to the over 1,000 ancient designs already discovered in the Nazca (or “Nasca”) and Palpa regions of southern Peru.
The Nazca Lines discovered so far consist of 800 straight lines, over 300 geometric designs and more than 70 animal and plant geoglyphs.

...

results.title: AI uncovers 303 new Nazca geoglyphs, including knife-wielding orca and alien figures in Peru | Archaeology News Online Magazine
excerpts:
# AI uncovers 303 new Nazca geoglyphs, including knife-wielding orca and alien figures in Peru
Researchers have used artificial intelligence (AI) to uncover over 300 previously unknown geoglyphs in the Nazca Desert of southern Peru.

...

This recent finding, led by Masato Sakai from Japan’s Yamagata University, nearly doubles the total number of known geoglyphs.
[AI uncovers 303 new Nazca geoglyphs, including knife-wielding orca and alien figures in Peru](https://archaeologymag.com/wp-content/uploads/ai-uncovers-303-new-nazca-geoglyphs-1_1.jpg) The 72-foot (22-meter) long “killer whale holding a knife”

...

In just six months, the AI-assisted study identified 303 new geoglyphs, adding to the 430 that had been discovered over nearly a century.

...

The AI model used in this study has already identified hundreds more potential geoglyph candidates that have yet to be examined. Researchers estimate that there could be as many as 250 additional geoglyphs awaiting discovery in the Nazca Desert.

results.title: AI-accelerated Nazca survey nearly doubles the number of known figurative geoglyphs and sheds light on their purpose | PNAS
excerpts:
# AI-accelerated Nazca survey nearly doubles the number of known figurative geoglyphs and sheds light on their purpose
## Abstract
It took nearly a century to discover a total of 430 figurative Nazca geoglyphs, which offer significant insights into the ancient cultures at the Nazca Pampa.
Here, we report the deployment of an AI system to the entire Nazca region, a UNESCO World Heritage site, leading to the discovery of 303 new figurative geoglyphs within only 6 mo of field survey, nearly doubling the number of known figurative geoglyphs.

...

## Previous Field Surveys.
Field surveys aided by aerial photography began in the 1940s and uncovered 112 figurative geoglyphs at the Nazca Pampa and surrounding areas ( 4 – 10 ). These consisted of 39 line-type and 73 relief-type geoglyphs. However, these studies did not cover the entire Nazca Pampa.

...

As a result, a total of 318 new figurative geoglyphs were discovered from 2004 to 2020. These consisted of 11 line-type and 307 relief-type geoglyphs.

...

## Results
Based on the above estimate, one may expect at least 248 additional AI-proposed figurative geoglyphs to be discovered from the Nazca Pampa upon completion of future field surveys. This estimate excludes additional finds in geoglyph groups and “non-AI” finds during the survey.
